# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — reuse prior-run measured champion (0.525 on these 40) + bounded fixes for its 7 regressions and 9 more failures
- Changes I made:
  - BASE: prompt.md + task_template.md = prior run's accepted cand_0001 (reused_seed_run), verbatim.
  - task_template Phase 2 snippet: read from `src` (data_only) and write to `wb`; convert leftover `=` cells in the target to cached values (clusters 1 and 6: 52541, 45707, 57354, 183-8).
  - task_template HOW TO WORK + Phase 3: only the first block runs; no invented output; no identical resend (print repr/type diagnostics instead) (cluster 2: 50811, 52541, 486-17, 12307, 203-15).
  - task_template CONTRACT 5: deleting whole rows/cols uses delete_rows/delete_cols, which shifts content (cluster 5: 28-7).
  - prompt.md §6 Excel semantics: case-insensitive matching, real today, TEXT codes / instruction example beats neighbours, blank only on a miss (9111, 534-26, 11276, 9391).
  - prompt.md §7 workbook-derived names and shape: header map, header = value kind, exact strings, finished-value shape, merged headers, membership filters, keyword categories, row ref stays key (50811, 188-39, 1925, 203-15, 279-23, 59160, 12307, 524-31, 45944).
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Keep the base's +12 fixes, and win back some of the 7 protected regressions.
  - Every new rule is conditional on its trigger. Trigger scans: delete → 6 val tasks (3 already use delete_*); today → 534-26 only; lookup-case → 11 tasks, framed as matching only, so written values are unchanged.
  - The snippet change is a bug fix.
- Building on prior RESULTS: the prior run's 0002–0005 were all rejected. I did NOT add mandatory steps, prune, add a blanket openpyxl rule, or an anti-relitigation clause.
- Refuted hypotheses: (from prior run) more mandatory phases; pruning the champion.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 38074, 59358 and others with no clear general cause; the 45944/12307 fixes are medium confidence.
- Plateau signal: n/a (iteration 1).
- Focus next iteration: read this RESULT's broke/fixed. If a §6/§7 rule broke a protected task, drop just that bullet. If resend loops persist, tighten the Phase 3 stop rule.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.700 Δ=+0.300 · fixed={11276, 12307, 290-1, 304-35, 38074, 409-45, 41978, 45707, 469-9, 50682, 524-31, 535-20, 56921, 58687, 59160, 59358} · broke={188-39, 374-31, 51680, 547-43} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

## Iteration cand_0002 — structural self-checks in the snippets (full target print, change-diff, None-recovery) + workbook-beats-prose decision table
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md §7 decision table "prose vs workbook → workbook wins" (spelling / formula-literal case / header column), keeping §6's format-example exception (203-15, 1925, 188-39).
  - prompt.md §7 bullets:
    - structured-ref worked example: `Table[@Col]` = search the table for the row key (45944);
    - the asker's formula range defines the data rows, side-by-side blocks (59129);
    - totals are not items (57354).
  - task_template Phase 1 snippet:
    - print all non-empty target cells when the range is ≤300 cells (`range_boundaries`);
    - header rows keyed by column letter;
    - build item lists from the header, never retype them (279-23, 547-43, 183-8).
  - task_template Phase 2 snippet: a diagnostic diff printing "k of N changed" and the pre-filled cells changed. Rules: 0 changed → re-read; a pre-filled change must be one the instruction asks for, and 2× means a total was summed (374-31, 57354).
  - task_template Phase 3:
    - a blank-on-miss check: a found 0 stays 0 (9391);
    - a recovery for targets still None: print the coordinates and keys from `ss`, no resend (183-8).
- Expected effect + safety: targets 10 of the 12 failures (51680 skipped, 59129 medium). All are conditional or diagnostic. The pre-filled diff is explicitly NOT a ban (10 passing tasks legitimately change pre-filled cells), and 0/40 val goldens equal their init, so the no-op guard is low risk.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 broke {188-39, 374-31, 51680, 547-43}; edits target 188-39, 374-31, 547-43. Not re-tried: mandatory phases, pruning, blanket openpyxl, anti-relitigation (prior-run rejects).
- Refuted hypotheses: none new.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 51680 (golden contradicts its own worked examples); 59129 if the range rule is not enough.
- Plateau signal: none yet (one accept, +0.300).
- Focus next iteration: use broke/fixed to attribute. If a passing task broke, suspect first the workbook-wins table (vs 11276-style format examples) or the pre-filled-diff wording, and drop just that piece.
